Dear all,
I am trying to estimate the european rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus) =
population of a Canary Island.=20
I use night counts on dirt roads to assess the population, I can only =
see the rabbits that are on the roads or close to them (less than 5 m at =
each size), because it is a very hilly place (slope between 20 to 45%) =
and vegetation tends to be relativly dense. Dirt roads run on all type =
of possible habitats that are found in the island.I would like to employ =
distance sampling using line transect with perpendicular distance.
My questions is:
Is it possible to assess the population of rabbits using only two =
categories of distance:=20
first between 0 to 4 meters, and the second between 4 to 8 meters?
Thanks a lot!

Francisco,
My reply won't help you with the basic question that you asked, but adds =
something else for you to consider. =20

It is quite possible that roads may effect rabbits in some way. Many =
species have some response to roads even if it is minor. Usually the =
vegetation adjacent to roads is different (or at least somewhat altered) =
from the vegetation of the surrounding landscape. This difference in =
vegetation can create habitat differences and effect the population of =
rabbits adjacent to roads. You may introduce considerable bias if you =
use roads for your line transects. You might want to read a paper that =
is in final draft for publication in Conservation Biology: The =
Ecological Effects of Roads on Terrestrial and Aquatic Communities: A =
Review , by Stephen C. Trombulak and Christopher A. Frissell. You might =
be able to get a copy from Chris Frissell (fris...@selway.umt.edu).

I realize that roads may be your best way of accessing the area, but you =
might want to do some sampling away from roads to reduce the bias.
